item.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to ceasefire in Ukrainian city hit by food crisis, brokered by Melania Trump
item.description:
SummaryCeasefire in Oleshky begins on Thursday, White House saysRussian commander says Moscow's forces to halt fire on TuesdayAccord allows humanitarian aid in and civilian evacuation through safe passageway, White House saysOleshky's remaining population totals 1,700 to 2,000 ​people, including about 50 children, White House saysWASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - US first lady Melania Trump ‌has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will begin next Thursday, the White House said on Friday.The chief of staff of Russian forces, Valery Gerasimov, said on the Defence Ministry's Telegram channel that Russian troops would halt fire from 4 a.m. local time (0100 GMT) on Tuesday to allow ​for the humanitarian operation to start.
Sign up here.Residents of the southern Ukrainian city, occupied by Russian forces since February 2022, have reported ​a deepening food crisis."Both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to ⁠enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway," a White House statement said.Ukraine's top negotiator, David Arakhamia, said on ​Telegram that the humanitarian operation would start once a ceasefire was in place.He said the accord, the result of a long process involving Melania ​Trump and Pope Leo, would set up a humanitarian corridor for residents to leave and allow assistance into the town.In Moscow, the Kremlin welcomed the agreement. It praised Melania Trump's role in securing the agreement and said President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin had discussed details.The Kremlin said earlier this week that work was ​under way to ease the humanitarian situation in Oleshky after Putin told the pope he was ready to cooperate on the issue.

item.title: Iran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if war resumes, officials say
item.description:
SummaryCompaniesIran plans wider retaliation if war resumes, officials sayIran threatens undersea cables, would try to stop repairsHormuz cable attacks could disrupt Gulf networksGlobal impact would be limited, analysts sayDUBAI, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the United States and Israel attack Iran again, two senior Iranian security officials ​told Reuters.Their comments followed warnings by Iranian officials that undersea cables in the region could become targets in any renewed conflict if diplomacy with Washington ‌collapses.
Sign up here.The two Iranian security officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, gave few details and did not say how or where exactly Tehran would carry out such attacks. But one of them said Iran would aim to prevent repairs after any attacks to prolong disruptions to communications, including internet connections."If Iran is attacked, there will be no more red lines ... from undersea cables to military bases, including covert ones," one ​of the officials said.The official warned Washington not to "play with fire", and said Iran had full access to the undersea cables and could easily destroy them.Yadollah ​Javani, the deputy head of political affairs for Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC), said on Wednesday that Iran could target seven major internet cables beneath ⁠the Strait of Hormuz if Iranian infrastructure came under attack.Undersea cables carry around 99% of global internet traffic, according to the International Telecommunication Union, a UN agency. But the ​global impact of such attacks by Iran could be limited as less than 1% of international bandwidth passes through the Strait of Hormuz, said Alan Mauldin, research director at telecommunications ​research firm TeleGeography.The strait separates Iran and Oman, linking the Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea.The US Department of State and Iran's Foreign Ministry did not respond to...

item.title: AI-discovered bugs may soon trigger fresh disruptions, cyber experts say
item.description:
Computer code is displayed on multiple screens in this illustration taken on October 22, 2026. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration Purchase Licensing Rights
, opens new tabSummaryCompaniesCloudflare CEO says 'a bunch of additional severe vulnerabilities' are currently being patchedOne cybersecurity expert said that, following PHP disclosures, 'there’s going to be a lot more fire drills'Experts split on whether more AI-found vulnerabilities will translate into more successful hacksWASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Advances in artificial intelligence have uncovered a stream of new software vulnerabilities that are almost ​certain to trigger more disruption along the lines of the outages that percolated across global government websites this week, according to seven cybersecurity professionals who spoke to ‌Reuters.AI helped drive a doubling of the number of digital flaws discovered year-on-year, according to research due to be published in the coming days by VulnCheck, a Massachusetts-based threat intelligence firm.
Sign up here.Matthew Prince, the chief executive of the digital infrastructure firm Cloudflare (NET.N)
, opens new tab, told Reuters he was aware of “a bunch of additional severe vulnerabilities that are present in other pieces of critical software” and predicted busy months ahead as AI surfaced long-hidden weaknesses in the ​fabric of the internet.“I think we’re going to have a couple years where every single week it’s going to feel like the sky is falling,” Prince said in an ​interview on Thursday.The outages that spread across government sites in Europe and elsewhere beginning on Wednesday happened after the discovery of weaknesses in PHP, ⁠a venerable programming language that powers a huge swath of the internet. item.title: France boosts police presence, hoping to prevent repeat of riots
item.description:
SummaryFrance deploys 70,000 police for Saturday protestsInterior minister accuses ultra-left of inciting violenceShooting by alleged Islamophobic gunman adds to tensionsMuseums, art events and businesses close over unrest fearsNational Rally congress in Orleans seen as possible flashpointPARIS, Oct 23 (Reuters) - France will deploy 70,000 police at nationwide protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Friday, looking ‌to prevent a repeat of the violence and looting that shocked the country last weekend.Elite security teams and heavily armed mobile squads will be mobilised alongside regular units in a show of force aimed at dispelling fears the government has lost control of the streets.
Sign up here."We will be uncompromising with rioters, looters and all those who commit acts of violence," Nunez told reporters, adding that "ultra-left" groups had been urging activists online to target public buildings and ​unleash more lawlessness."We are not talking about a nice, friendly demonstration," Nunez said. "We are ready for tomorrow. We will be extremely vigilant, extremely firm, and we will let ​absolutely nothing pass."
SHOOTING SPREE NEAR PARIS ADDS TO TENSIONS Anger over living costs and strained public services has drawn students, workers and unions onto the ⁠streets in recent weeks, but authorities say radical militants and bands of young looters have taken advantage of the dispute to sow chaos.Some far-right politicians have blamed migrants and radical Islam ​for the turmoil. President Emmanuel Macron has dismissed such accusations.Ratcheting up the tensions, a man, who officials suspect was motivated by Islamophobic hatred, opened fire from a car west of Paris on Friday, ​killing one person and wounding four others, including a 12-year-old girl."(It was) objectively a racist attack," said local mayor Ali Rabeh, blaming far-right rhetoric for inflaming tensions.Police have authorised only one union demonstration in Paris on Saturday, reject...

item.title: Macron says Paris suburb shooting that killed one person was terrorist and racist act
item.description:
SummaryGunman kills one and wounds five, including 12-year-old girlSuspect named as Kevin TMacron: shooting was 'terrorist and racist'Macron: shooting marks turning point for FranceShooting comes amid heightened tensions after ​protestsPARIS, Oct 23 (Reuters) - A gunman killed one person and wounded ‌five others, including a 12-year-old girl, in a shooting in a Paris suburb that French President Emmanuel Macron described as a "terrorist and racist" attack."What happened today is, I am telling you, a turning point, because it is the first ​time we have had a terrorist act that was planned to kill our compatriots, our ​children, based on the colour of their skin or their religion," Macron told ⁠reporters.
Sign up here.The shooting happened earlier on Friday when the gunman fired an automatic weapon at a petrol station, ​a medical centre and a children's playground in Trappes, on the Paris outskirts.Officials said a 39-year-old suspect, ​whom they named as Kevin T, had been arrested. His family surname was not given, as is common practice in such criminal inquiries in France.The shooting comes at a moment of particular tension in France, after nationwide protests turned violent ​last Saturday and before further demonstrations this coming weekend.Some far-right politicians have blamed immigration for looting and ​vandalism in a number of French cities on October 17.Macron said the gunman had deliberately chosen not to fire ‌upon ⁠some people due to their skin colour and appearance.

item.description:

Jordan's health ​minister said 40 people were wounded.
Sign up here.Interior Minister Mazin Al Farrayeh said the attack had been carried out by "extremists", but that it was too ​early to tell whether they had any links to known groups either inside or outside Jordan.Such attacks are extremely ⁠rare in Jordan, which is relatively stable, though Jordanian authorities say they have repeatedly foiled attempted attacks by Islamist militants in recent years.There was no ​immediate claim of responsibility.A video aired on Jordan's state-owned Al-Mamlaka television station that appeared to be from a security camera mounted on the church showed three ​people firing at it from a sidewalk and hiding behind trees and a low wall. The video showed the attackers then running towards the church's entrance. Reuters was able to verify the video from the entry path and wall surrounding the church, as well as other details."This is a result of a terrorist ideology and blind extremism and ​we will not allow society to go down...

item.title: First Russian diesel from Putin-Trump deal heading for US, data shows
item.description:
The current price of diesel fuel is displayed at a gas station in Encinitas, California, US, October 21, 2026. REUTERS/Mike Blake Purchase Licensing Rights
, opens new tabSummaryTanker with 40,000 tons of diesel bound for New YorkExpected to arrive on November 7First US imports of Russian petroleum product since 2022 banRussia to send initial 300,000 tons to US, global markets -TrumpBuyer and seller not known yetOct 23 (Reuters) - The first Russian diesel bound for the US following a surprise agreement reached between Moscow and ‌US President Donald Trump is aboard a tanker heading for New York, ship-tracking data showed on Friday.Trump announced the deal this month as part of his efforts to bring down soaring diesel prices ahead of November 3 US midterm elections.
Sign up here.Trump also waived parts of a new US sanctions law against Russia and ​threatened Europe with a US diesel export ban unless countries released more from their emergency reserves to help ease prices.The ​Malta-flagged medium-sized tanker Agioi Fanendes was loaded with 40,000 metric tons of ultra-low sulphur diesel in Russia's ⁠Baltic port of Primorsk on October 22, according to LSEG shipping data. It is expected to arrive in the United States ​on November 7.The identity of the buyer and seller were not immediately known. The cargo will be the first imported by the ​US since former President Joe Biden announced a ban on US imports of Russian oil and petroleum products in 2022.Trump announced on October 9 that Russia would immediately export 300,000 metric tons, or 2.25 million barrels, to the US and global markets, followed by 500,000 tons in November and 1 million ​tons "immediately thereafter".A Kremlin spokesperson on Friday confirmed a first ship under the deal had departed, but did not specify whether it was ​bound for the US market or elsewhere."As far as I'm aware, there have already been reports from the Ministry of Energy that the first ‌tanker has, ⁠in fact, set sail for ...

Oct 23 (Reuters) - A Utah judge is expected to set on Friday a trial date for Tyler Robinson, the former electrical apprentice accused of killing prominent right-wing activist Charlie Kirk, ​with the defendant requesting a 2029 date and Kirk's widow ‌calling for a trial next year.Judge Tony Graf will open a hearing at 1 p.m. (1900 GMT) to decide a date to start the high-profile, capital trial of Robinson, who allegedly shot Kirk ​as he debated with students at a Utah university in September ​2025.
Sign up here.Utah prosecutors are seeking the death penalty for Robinson and ⁠requested a January 31, 2028, start date for a trial they expect to last 17 ​weeks, according to their scheduling memo.Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to seven ​counts, including aggravated murder, for allegedly shooting Kirk as he held one of his trademark debates at Utah Valley University in Orem.In a legal filing, Robinson's lawyers said they ​expected a six-to-seven-month trial and requested it start in the third quarter of ​2029. They said Robinson's case required years of preparation due to voluminous evidence and issues ‌such ⁠as the venue, jury selection and witnesses.Kirk's widow Erika said the defense request was "grossly out of line with comparable cases" and asked that the trial start as early as possible next year, preferably no later than October 4, according ​to a legal filing.Charlie ​Kirk was a ⁠polarizing figure in US politics. ISTANBUL, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Prime Minister Mark Carney on Friday dismissed accusations that Canada planned to interfere in next month's US midterm elections and said he was disappointed ​in comments made by the American ambassador.Carney's remarks underline the chilly state of ‌bilateral relations since Canada walked away from talks on a possible trade deal in late August, citing unreasonable US demands.
Sign up here.The US embassy in Canada on Wednesday said Ottawa "brushes off concerns about potential interference ​in US elections, even as its ministers and premiers openly describe plans to ​influence American politics."A week earlier, Ambassador Pete Hoekstra had told a ⁠podcast that his message to Canadians was to "keep your nose out of American politics."Carney ​said Canada had no intention of interfering in the November 3 elections."There is no merit ​to these claims," he told reporters during an official visit to Turkey. "I'm disappointed their envoy sees that as his role to make these suggestions."US President Donald Trump has imposed a raft of tariffs on imports ​from Canada and frequently suggests he could annex the country. item.title: Health officials race to trace source of Nigeria's Ebola infection
item.description:
SummaryHealth officials probe source of Nigeria's first Ebola case in a decadeFour-country outbreak raises fears of wider spread across AfricaQuestions grow over possible infection link to UgandaUganda says it is Ebola-freeDAKAR/NAIROBI, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria's first Ebola patient in more ‌than a decade became infected, amid fears the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.The Swiss government said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda, Kenya ​and now Nigeria.
Sign up here.The Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs said the woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband ​in Uganda, which the World Health Organization declared Ebola-free in August.The outbreak has now been reported in four countries across ⁠eastern, central and western Africa, giving it the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date.The possibility that the Nigerian patient ​became infected in Uganda, where officials say she spent a two-week holiday before returning to Abuja, has fuelled concerns about undetected transmission in a country where ​the outbreak had appeared to be under control.Ugandan authorities have said the woman had been in eastern Congo before transiting through Uganda, but both the WHO and Africa's top health body say that information has yet to be confirmed.The WHO said investigations were continuing to establish the source of the infection. Nigerian authorities tested the woman for Ebola ​13 days after she fell ill in Abuja.
